title: Chapter 29: Natsuki Subaru’s Restart
content:
Chapter 29:

Natsuki Subaru’s Restart

—All that existed there was “nothingness.”

Dimly, that consciousness casually looked around. Though “looked around” wasn’t an appropriate expression in this case.

The consciousness possessed no eyes. Furthermore, it had no hands, no feet, no body parts at all. It was merely a state where an uncertain thing—an incorporeal consciousness—floated there.

Understanding nothing, conveying nothing, it looked around.

A dark, completely empty room. A world shrouded in pitch black, where the boundary between ceiling and wall was indiscernible, making it impossible to even guess the room’s size.

Suddenly, meaning was born into that world of everlasting darkness.

In the position corresponding to the consciousness’s front, a human silhouette abruptly appeared.

A slender, indistinct outline, its body likewise cloaked in pitch black. A haze obscured everything from the upper body upwards, strongly impeding the consciousness’s ability to recognize it.

With the appearance of the silhouette, the consciousness gained a sensation for the first time.

And before that sensation could fade, the shadow moved slowly, reaching out as if trying to convey something to the consciousness.

It didn’t understand. Nothing was conveyed.

Even so, for some reason, it couldn’t tear its attention away from the silhouette—.

“—We cannot meet yet.”

Leaving behind that faint whisper, the world abruptly vanished.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

The moment he woke up, the first strong thought Subaru had was, 

Thank you for giving birth to me with such a sturdy body, Mom and Dad.

He had thrown himself off a cliff, plummeting headfirst straight toward the ground. There was no doubt the impact had nearly snapped his cervical spine clean off, but eternal rest didn’t visit Subaru instantaneously in that state—far from it.

“To think I couldn’t die instantly and was still a little conscious… That’s way past the level of just being unlucky.”

Right next to the corpse of the horned beast who had died from the fall, he spent the countdown to his own death completely immobilized and tormented by excruciating pain.

He could guess he probably didn’t last very long before dying, but the subjective time of the experience made it feel like hours.

Just thinking about the unbearable possibility of Beatrice coming down to check on him and healing him while he was still breathing made him shudder.

“I’m absolutely never dying by my own hand again. I wouldn’t do it even if it kills me.”

Even the moments leading up to that, just remembering his internal monologue made him literally want to die.

Acting so cool on the outside while being that terrified on the inside. He couldn’t possibly call that a resolute decision.

However—,

“I made it… back…”

Reaching out his hand and clenching his fist, Subaru confirmed his current whereabouts.

A soft bed. Tidied sheets. Even the reddish-brown, samue-like outfit felt nostalgic, and then—,

“Sister, Sister. It seems our guest is still half-asleep.”

“Rem, Rem. It seems our guest has gone senile at a rather young age.”

The twin girls were holding hands, staring at Subaru with two pairs of eyes from in front of the bed.

Familiar voices and familiar gestures. An intense greeting that had been repeated four times before, making this the fifth.

He had a mountain of things he wanted to say. There were so many feelings he wanted to voice that they pierced his chest. And yet, it was as if they were stuck in his throat, and none of them would come out.

Seeing Rem alive and well, seeing Ram’s endlessly rude attitude, and feeling the two of them treat him like it was perfectly normal, an overwhelming emotion welled up inside him.

“Guest, Guest, what is the matter? Are you feeling unwell?”

“Guest, Guest, is something wrong? Did you have an attack from a chronic illness?”

Right after seeing their faces, Subaru fell silent and clutched his chest, confusing the twins. Splitting to the left and right, they approached the bed and reached out as if to comfort the crouching Subaru.

And so, as the two drew near, Subaru—

“Yoink.”

“Eh.”

“Ah.”

Uttering a sound effect out loud, he pulled the twins in with all his might and hugged them tight.

Blue hair on the right, pink hair on the left; one arm each was plenty to wrap around their petite bodies. Burying his face between the twins, who had essentially been shoved head-to-head in front of him, he savored the feeling of their hair against his cheeks as he spoke.

“Ahhh, I’m back—I made it back. Finally, back in this place, keeping these exact same feelings. I’m! Ho-! Me!”

He roughly nuzzled his face against their heads, then patted their backs and released them.

The two couldn’t completely hide their dismay at Subaru’s sudden embrace, but they quickly regained their senses and sprang away from the bed.

“Sister, Sister, our guest has made me his plaything.”

“Rem, Rem, we have been made the targets of our guest’s bestial lust.”

“Hah, that’s where you’re wrong. Hate to break it to you both, but unfortunately, you’re both just a tiny, subtle bit outside my strike zone. Remember this. I’m not really into the younger-girl trope! And for girls, it’s gotta be long hair, long!”

A girl’s femininity resided in her hair—that was Subaru’s pet theory.

Therefore, a woman’s hair should be long. And a silver-haired heroine was absolute justice for Subaru. Plus, if it came with an older-sister vibe who’d let him act a little spoiled, he’d have no complaints. Hence,

“Emilia-tan is the fastball right down the middle of my strike zone! Sorry, but you guys are off-center. Still a nice pitch, though!”

“Sister, Sister. I do not quite understand his remarks, but we are being insulted.”

“Rem, Rem. His words are insane, but I feel we are being disparaged.”

The twins’ response to Subaru’s rapid-fire rambling was rather harsh.

However, brushing off their attitude, Subaru sprang up from the bed. He stood barefoot on the floor and executed a sharp spin right on the spot. Turning back around in the center of the room, he pointed the fingers of both hands at the two who were still standing frozen by the bed.

“Now listen, hey listen, listen to me. Give each other lap pillows, clean out your earholes, and listen up good.”

He held his palms out toward the silent pair, adding in useless gestures of opening and closing his hands as he continued.

“Given the circumstances, I know you guys must have, well, all sorts of bizarre and complicated backgrounds. I totally get it, but I’m gonna be super blunt with you.”

As if gauging him, the twins silently urged him to continue.

He figured they had probably already started evaluating him at this point. Being aware of their gaze and trying to win their trust through painful trial and error—he wasn’t capable of thinking up something that clever.

To begin with, he was hopelessly terrible at socializing.

If he possessed the high-level communication skills to read people’s moods and take the appropriate action on the spot, he wouldn’t have become a shut-in, and he would have managed things much better over here, too.

So even knowing the meaning behind their sharp gazes, there wasn’t much Subaru could do. His informational advantage was negligible anyway.

Therefore, what Subaru was about to say to them right now was not a declaration of war, but purely a personal vow.

In other words,

“I believe in you guys, so let’s get along!”

Just like the first time, he would just face them as earnestly as he could.

Subaru was sure he had felt the same way on his very first day summoned to this other world.

Even if he knew what future awaited him, he didn’t possess the power to fully capitalize on it. In that case, to make the most of the chances he was given, he had no choice but to live and struggle through the situations right in front of him with everything he had.

The twins’ eyes widened at Subaru’s proposal, and they exchanged glances, communicating wordlessly with one another. There was no way to know what was being said during that silent exchange, but Subaru wasn’t docile enough to meekly wait for their verdict either.

Especially since, this time around, he had decided to leave that docility behind.

“Leaving me out is so lonely, you meanies! The world is much wider and more open than that. So stop immersing yourselves in your own little world and let’s open up more! With who? With me!”

“Sister, Sister. Our awakened guest is incredibly bothersome.”

“Rem, Rem. Our finally awakened guest is annoying to death.”

“But you still have to serve such an annoying, bothersome me with the utmost sincerity! Wow, it’s been a while since I felt like a guest! It’s fleeting, but it feels great, yeah!”

He felt like his tension was exploding, overcompensating for all the gloom that had built up inside him.

Relying on a mouth that was running faster than usual, Subaru’s tongue fired off flippant remarks with even more reckless abandon. Then,

“—Couldn’t you wake up just a little more quietly?”

The voice came from the direction of the entrance.

Looking over, standing right by the door was a silver-haired girl. She gave the already open door a light knock and furrowed her beautiful brows in exasperation,

“I’m glad to see you’re energetic, but you’re still recovering, so you shouldn’t be making such a racket.”

“Don’t worry, Emilia-tan is my number one star!”

“What are you talking about?!”

He gave a thumbs-up, flashing his teeth with a triumphant, striking pose.

Faced with Subaru’s full-force action, Emilia put a hand to her forehead,

“Umm…”

Her gaze wandered as if searching for the right words, and then,

“Anyway, good morning. I’m glad you’re safe.”

Emilia smiled in relief.

Returning a nod to her smile, Subaru also pulled up the corners of his mouth,

“Yeah, good morning. —Well then, shall we begin?”

Unable to understand the intent behind Subaru’s remark, the three girls tilted their heads in confusion.

Smiling wryly at them, Subaru waved his hand and,

“One week at Roswaal Manor—the playthrough starts now.”

Declared it, speaking to no one else but himself, as if making a vow.

—Now, let’s get this story moving.

To look up at the morning Subaru wished for, with the people Subaru wished for.

The fifth iteration of day one. Morning at Roswaal Manor began.
